title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the paper and in the header of each page.

analysis.description: This paper introduces ADEPT, a semantic plausibility task that involves assessing changes in event plausibility due to adjectival modifiers. The task consists of over 16,000 sentences with human annotations and evaluates the performance of transformer-based models against human judgments.

type.justification: The study involves the creation of a dataset and empirical evaluation of transformer-based models' performance on the task compared to human performance.
type.quote: Our experiments suggest a persistent performance gap between human annotators and large language representation models, with the latter exhibiting a lower sensitivity to context.

name.justification: The paper focuses on language models, sentence plausibility, and understanding the effects of adjectives on context, all of which are key aspects of Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Discerning the varying effects of adjectival modifiers on the reading of a sentence is critical in a variety of tasks involving natural language understanding.

name.justification: The main task introduced is centered around judging the plausibility of sentences based on adjectival modifiers, which is directly related to semantic plausibility.
name.quote: We develop ADEPT, a semantic plausibility task that features over 16 thousand instances consisting of two sentences.

name.justification: The paper evaluates the performance of transformer-based models like BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa on the ADEPT task.
name.quote: Powerful, massively pre-trained language models (LMs) have pushed the performance on various natural language understanding benchmarks... transformer architectures including BERT and RoBERTa.

name.justification: RoBERTa is explicitly mentioned as one of the models evaluated in the research study.
name.quote: RoBERTa (Liu et al., 2019) is an improved variant of BERT that adds more training data with larger batch sizes and longer training.

is_contributed.justification: RoBERTa was used in experiments to evaluate its performance but it was not developed in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: transformer architectures including BERT and RoBERTa are believed to perform at near human-level performance on a number of Natural Language Inference (NLI) tasks.

is_executed.justification: RoBERTa was executed as part of the experiment to determine model performance on ADEPT.
is_executed.quote: We evaluate several transformer-based models on ADEPT.

is_compared.justification: RoBERTa's performance is compared to other models like BERT and DeBERTa and to human performance.
is_compared.quote: Of the transformer models, the highest 3-class accuracy is achieved by DeBERTa and the highest 5-class accuracy by RoBERTa.
